summary: Real, dated pain from Etsy's July 2026 DDP rule, but no evidence anyone pays a third party when Etsy's free estimator exists and may soon add bulk apply. Etsy-seller tools keep failing on willingness to pay and this one adds liability for wrong duty estimates.

demand.evidence: Problem well sourced (valueaddedresource.net, alura.io) and sellers are pausing US sales, but RESEARCH.md found no paid tool, no price and no one asking to pay; prices are the researcher's own proposal.

statusQuo.evidence: Free Etsy/Zonos estimator one listing at a time with no variations, or spreadsheets, or padding shipping. Rule is four months old so many sellers have already adapted; Etsy may ship bulk apply.

specificity.evidence: Target is a category (non-US handmade sellers with 20-300 variation listings); no named person or heard consequence, and unknown whether they would pay rather than raise prices.

wedge.evidence: CSV in, CSV out, no API or login, weekend build; but value depends on HS code and rate accuracy the seller cannot verify, and pure margin arithmetic is a spreadsheet.

futureFit.evidence: One-time re-price that erodes as Etsy and Zonos improve native tooling; rate alerts would help but are a larger, different product.

premises: Non-US sellers have a recurring painful re-pricing task: supported but shrinking after the first months.
A third party will be paid for what Etsy gives free: unsupported.
A solo-built estimate with LLM HS guesses is trustworthy enough to price from: weak.
Etsy will not add bulk or variation support soon: unsupported.
Sellers have unit cost and weight data at hand: unverified.
alternatives: Minimal: free single-page calculator plus Sheets template posted in seller communities, email capture for bulk CSV.
Ideal: ongoing duty-rate and margin monitor across marketplaces with alerts (large, high risk).
Extend: bundle with the packpass audience (same non-US Etsy seller segment) rather than a standalone product.
wedge: A free no-upload calculator (cost, duty, DDP fee, Etsy fees to US price), with a one-time $19-29 bulk CSV only if people ask.

feasibility.notes: Next.js on Vercel Hobby, pure priceVariation() with Vitest, static rates.json, papaparse. Proving test: cost 20, duty 10%, DDP 15, fees, 30% target margin returns 30.00% within 0.01. Ongoing cost is hand-maintaining rates.json.

risks: Etsy or Zonos ships bulk/variation-aware estimator
Wrong HS code or duty rate costs the seller money; liability
Sellers stop US sales instead of buying a tool
Etsy exports lack cost and weight, adding input friction
Unproven willingness to pay, same weakness as earlier Etsy-seller ideas
killCriteria: Etsy or Zonos ships bulk/variation apply; under 5% of 200 qualified visitors start an upload; under 10 reach pay or pre-pay $19 in two weeks; sellers say they have already re-priced.

landing.headline: Re-price every Etsy variation for US duty in one upload
landing.subhead: Upload your listings CSV and get a US price per variation that keeps your margin after duty, DDP fees and Etsy fees.
bullets: Per-variation prices, not one listing at a time
Margin-safe after duty, DDP fee and Etsy fees
Flags listings not worth shipping to the US
CSV export to paste back into Etsy
landing.audience: Non-US Etsy sellers with 20-300 listings who sell to the US

launch.post: Non-US Etsy sellers: how are you re-pricing variations for the DDP rule? Etsy's estimator does one listing at a time. I'm testing a bulk tool: {url}. Would you pay for it, and what would you need to trust the numbers?
